The one date is verified: the code of today deletes the images of a closed run 30 days after it closed (packages/service/src/work.ts:695, apps/web/src/operations/index.ts:56), and the storage form of today came on 2026-10-04 (commits 6219fdf and 0b629ce), so the first deletion is not before 2026-11-03. This code is in production now, so the date does not depend on the implementation.

The ids D-PRE-33 to D-PRE-39 are not used.

decisions.question: How does the contract take the settled UI design of the lab?
decisions.options: (1) with-each-page: no line now; each UI pull request changes the contract lines that its page replaces. (2) rule-by-reference: one map row says that the pages follow the settled lab design at one tag, names 5 verified reversals, and names what does not change. (3) rules-in-contract: write each changed UI rule into the contract, so that the lab branch can go. (4) layout-out: one line says that the contract binds behavior only, and layout and look are not contract rules.
decisions.recommended: rule-by-reference. It is the smallest text that makes the design an approved rule before the first UI pull request, and contract line 192 already has this form (it names pull request #184 and what it replaced). It is wrong if the lab branch is deleted after the build (then rules-in-contract), or if the maintainer wants no layout in the contract (then layout-out: RULE-05, RULE-09, and RULE-02 show that the app already differs from three UI rules).

decisions.question: Does the audit report the two tested CSS rewrites to Ariakit UI, and in which form?
decisions.options: (1) no-report: nothing is written in ariakit/ariakit; the facts stay in apps/lab/audit/reports/perf/record. (2) issue: one public issue in ariakit/ariakit with the two rewrites as text, the numbers, and the limits. (3) pull-request: one pull request in ariakit/ariakit with rewrite 1 (two class names of nav.ts) and rewrite 3 (two custom variants of ui.css, 63 selectors).
decisions.recommended: issue. It keeps the two measured facts where the owner of the code finds them, costs about one hour (estimate), and changes no code. The two hover rules are still on the branch main of ariakit/ariakit today (nav.ts lines 391 and 395, read with gh). It is wrong if the authorization is for the service work only and no public text with numbers from one browser and a lab copy is wanted (then no-report), or if the change is wanted now (then pull-request, after the tests of Ariakit).
